summary: The root رعي primarily means to guard, preserve, or pasture animals, implying careful oversight. It extends to observing, considering, or taking care of something, like a promise or a right.

provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: رَعَتِ المَاشِيَةُ , aor. تَرْعَى, (Msb, K,) inf. n. رَعْىٌ (S, * Msb, K) and رِعَايَةٌ (K) and مَرْعًى; (S, * K, * JM;) and, and; (K;) The cattle [ pastured, or] pastured by themselves. (Msb.) And رَعَتِ المَاشِيَةُ الكَلَأَ, inf. n. رَعْىٌ (Mgh, TA) and رِعَايَةٌ [and مَرْعًى ]; and, and; [ The cattle pastured upon, or depastured, the herbage; ] all signifying the same: (TA:) and of a camel you say, رَعَى الكَلَأَ بِنَفْسِهِ, inf. n.
inf. n. تَرْعِيَةٌ, He said [ of him ], رَعَاهُ ٱللّٰهُ [ May God keep him, or guard him: or he said to him, رَعَاكَ ٱللّٰهُ May God keep thee, or guard thee ]. (TA.)

راعى الحِمَارُ الحُمُرَ The ass pastured with the [other] asses: (S, K:) and in like manner one says of camels with wild animals. (TA.) راعت الأَرْضُ, a reading required by the context in the K, is wrong; the correct phrase being ارعت الأَرْضُ [q. v.]. (TA.) See also 1, in the latter half of the paragraph, in eight places. المُرَاعَاةُ is also syn. with المُنَاظَرَةُ [app.

ارعى المَاشِيَةَ i. q. رَعَاهَا: see 1, in the former half of the paragraph. Said of God, it means He caused to grow, for the cattle, that upon which they might pasture. (S.) One says also ارعت الأَرْضُ, [as though المَاشِيَةَ or the like were understood] The land abounded [as though it fed abundantly] with herbage: (Zj, K:) راعت الأَرْضُ, in this sense [as stated above, see 3,] is wrong. (TA.) And ارعاهُ المَكَانَ He made the place to be a pasturage for him.
تَرَعَّىَ see 1, first and second sentences.
إِرْتَعَىَ see 1, in three places, first two sentences.

[app. signifies He desired cattle to pasture: and hence, he left them to pasture alone ]. You say, اِسْتَرْعَيْتُ مَالِىَ القَمَرَ, meaning I left my cattle to pasture without a pastor to take care of them in the night: and [in like manner,] استرعيتهُ الشَّمْسَ, in the day. (TA in art. قمر.) اِسْتَرْعَيْتُهُ الشَّىْءَ (S, K *) I asked him, or desired him, to keep or guard, or be mindful of or regardful of, the thing.

and Pasture, or herbage; (S, Mgh, K;) the food of beasts: (Msb:) pl. of the former أَرْعَآءٌ [meaning kinds, or sorts, of pasture or herbage ]: (K:) and of ↓ the latter مَرَاعٍ. (Msb.) It is said in a prov., وَلَا كَالسَّعْدَانِ [ Pasture, but not like the سعدان: see art. سعد ].

a subst. from 1 in the first of the senses mentioned in this art.; i. e. [The act of cattle's pasturing, or their pasturing alone, ] from رَعَتِ المَاشِيَةُ. (K.) [Also The act, or occupation, of keeping or tending, or of pasturing or feeding, animals.] You say [of a man], يُجِيدُ رِعْيَةَ الإِبِلِ [ He performs well the act of keeping or tending, or of pasturing or feeding, camels ].

and رُعْوَى: see the next paragraph. [Both seem to be also substs. from أَرْعَيْتُ عَلَيْهِ; and thus to be syn. with بَقْوَى and بُقْوَى; and in like manner, is probably syn. with بُقْيَا: the radical ى being changed into و as it is in بقوى.] You say, مَا لِى عَلَيْهِ رَعْوَى وَلَا بَقْوَى [ I have no mercy nor pity to bestow upon him ]. (JK in art. بقى. [See بُقْيَا.]) See also 1 in art. رعو [from which رَعْوَى in this phrase may also with reason be regarded as derivable].

a subst. from رَعَى as used in the phrase رَعَى أَمْرَهُ [expl. in the first paragraph; thus signifying Mindfulness, regardfulness, or observance, of an affair, or a case]; as also and. (K.) See also the next preceding paragraph. And see art. رعو.

[ رَعِىٌّ Pastured: ruled, or governed: and kept, or guarded: so accord. to Golius, as on the authority of the KL; but not in my copy of that work. It is agreeable with analogy as syn. with مَرْعِىٌّ: and from it is formed the subst. next following.]

[with ة affixed لِلنَّقْلِ, i. e., to transfer the word from the category of epithets to that of substantives,] Cattle pasturing, or pasturing by themselves: and cattle kept, tended, or pastured: (K, TA:) pl.
رعاءة الخَيْلِ : see رَاعِيَةٌ.

and رُعَاوَى Camels that pasture around the people and their dwellings (S, K) because they are those upon which they work [or perform their business ]: (S:) but in the Tekmileh it is written, as meaning cattle that pasture around the dwellings of the people. (TA.)
: see رَعِيَّةٌ.
: see رَعَاوَى.

[act. part. n. of 1]. You say مَاشِيَةٌ رَاعِيَةٌ Cattle [ pasturing, or] pasturing by themselves: (Msb:) pl. رَوَاعِى [a mistranscription for رَوَاعٍ ]. (TA.) رَاعِى البُسْتَانِ and الأُتُنِ are names of Two species of جَنَادِب [or locusts ]; (K;) the latter mentioned by ISd: Sgh says that the former is a large جُنْدَب: and the latter is another species, that does not fly.

[fem. of رَاعٍ. Also a subst. formed from the latter word by the affix ة; like رَعِيَّةٌ from رَعِىٌّ ]: see راعٍ, third sentence. الرَّاعِيَةُ is the name of A certain bird: (TA:) [and] so is رَاعِيَةُ الخَيْلِ; (TA, and thus in some copies of the K;) thus correctly written, as in the Tekmileh; in [some of] the copies of the K, راعية الجبل; [perhaps the same as the former bird;] a yellow bird, that is found beneath the bellies of horses or similar beasts; thus in the Tekmileh; said…

[app. More, and most, merciful or compassionate; from أَرْعَيْتُ عَلَيْهِ, though by rule it should be formed from an unaugmented verb accord. to many of the grammarians: and hence, being nearly syn. with أَرْفَقُ in the primary sense, syn. with this latter, or nearly so, in a secondary sense]. You say, أَمْرُ كَ َا أَرْفَقُ بِى وَأَرْعَى عَلَىَّ [app. meaning (assumed tropical:) This affair is more, or most, easy and convenient to me ]. (TA.)
The yoke that is placed upon the necks of the two bulls employed in ploughing; (AA, Sgh, K, TA;) of the dial. of Azd-Shanoo-ah. (TA.)
: see رَعِيَّةٌ.
: see what next follows.

and تُرْعِيَّةٌ (Fr, S, ISd, K) and تَرْعِيَّةٌ, (ISd, K,) and sometimes without teshdeed, (K,) the first without teshdeed mentioned by Sgh on the authority of Fr, (TA,) and (S, K) and (Sgh as from Fr) and (Sgh, K) and and (K) A man who performs well the act of keeping or tending, or of pasturing or feeding, camels: (S, K:) or whose habitual work, or occupation, or the habitual work, or occupation, of whose fathers, is, or has been, the tending, or pasturing, of camels: (ISd, K:)…
: see what next precedes.
: see what next precedes.

an inf. n. of 1 [q. v.]. (S, K.) And A pasturage, or place of pasture; (S, K;) as also: (Sgh, K:) pl. مَرَاعٍ. (TA.) [Hence,] لَا تَدَعَنَّ فَتَاةً وَلَا فَإِنَّ لِكُلٍّ بُغَاةٌ [ Do not thou leave uncared for a young woman nor a pasturage, for there are persons that seek, or endeavour, to find and get each ]: a prov. enjoining the availing oneself of an opportunity, and the setting about an affair with prudence, discretion, precaution, or sound judgment.
: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places.
[ Kept, or tended; pastured, or fed: kept, guarded, or minded: and] ruled, or governed; as in an ex. above, voce رَاعٍ, last sentence but one. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
